chunk: Performance Review & Appraisal Policy (EN, 202501, Expanded) # Performance Review & Appraisal Policy Company: Global Service Firm Region: Global (EN) Version: 202501

The Performance Review & Appraisal Policy establishes a structured process for evaluating employee performance, aligning individual goals with organizational objectives, and facilitating career development. This policy applies to all employees across all regions and levels within Global Service Firm.
Frequency: Conducted once a year. Timing: Typically scheduled in Q4 to align with yearend evaluations. Focus: Comprehensive assessment of employee performance over the past year.
Frequency: Conducted once a year, midway through the annual cycle. Timing: Typically scheduled in Q2. Focus: Progress check on goals, adjustments as necessary, and feedback on performance.
Frequency: Conducted at the end of the probationary period (usually 36 months). Focus: Evaluation of new hires to determine fit and performance.

Performance will be evaluated on a scale of 1 to 5, with detailed behavioral anchors for each rating: | Rating | Description | Behavioral Anchors | |||| | 1 | Unsatisfactory | Consistently fails to meet job requirements; lacks necessary skills; does not respond to feedback. | | 2 | Needs Improvement | Occasionally meets expectations but often falls short; requires supervision to complete tasks; limited engagement. | | 3 | Meets Expectations | Consistently meets job requirements; completes tasks effectively; demonstrates adequate skills and engagement. | | 4 | Exceeds Expectations | Often exceeds job requirements; takes initiative; actively contributes to team success; positively influences others. | | 5 | Outstanding | Consistently exceeds job requirements; demonstrates exceptional skills; leads initiatives; serves as a role model for others. |

1 (Unsatisfactory): An employee fails to complete assigned projects on time and does not respond to constructive feedback. 3 (Meets Expectations): An employee consistently meets deadlines and collaborates well with team members. 5 (Outstanding): An employee not only meets all objectives but also introduces innovative solutions that enhance team productivity.

section: Goal Setting and Alignment with Company Strategy
chunk: Employees will set SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Timebound) goals aligned with company objectives during the annual review.

section: Goal Setting and Alignment with Company Strategy
chunk: 1. Initial Discussion: Managers and employees discuss company goals and how individual contributions align. 2. Drafting Goals: Employees draft their goals using the SMART criteria. 3. Review and Finalization: Goals are reviewed and finalized in collaboration with the manager.

section: Goal Setting and Alignment with Company Strategy
chunk: Goal: Increase client satisfaction ratings by 15% by Q4 through improved communication and service delivery.

To foster a culture of continuous improvement, managers are encouraged to provide ongoing feedback outside of formal review periods. This includes: Regular checkins (monthly or biweekly). Constructive feedback on specific projects or tasks. Recognition of achievements in realtime.
Actively participate in the review process. Set and pursue development goals. Seek feedback and guidance from managers.
Provide regular feedback and support. Conduct performance reviews and document outcomes. Facilitate the goalsetting process.
Provide training and resources for managers and employees. Ensure compliance with the performance review process. Maintain performance documentation.
Review performance ratings for consistency and fairness across departments. Address discrepancies in ratings.

All performance reviews must be documented using the official review forms. Documentation should include: Completed review forms. Goalsetting forms. Notes from feedback sessions. Any relevant performance data.
Performance reviews will identify training and development needs, linking them to: Professional development opportunities. Training programs that align with individual career aspirations.
Performance ratings will directly influence: Promotion eligibility. Salary adjustments and bonuses. Recognition programs.

1. Identify Issues: Managers should identify specific areas of concern. 2. Feedback Session: Conduct a meeting to discuss performance issues and expectations. 3. Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): If necessary, develop a PIP with clear objectives and timelines. 4. FollowUp: Regularly check in on progress and provide support.
Underperformance: An employee consistently misses deadlines. The manager schedules a feedback session to discuss the issue, sets a PIP with specific deadlines, and checks in weekly.

Employees who disagree with their performance rating may appeal the decision by: 1. Submitting a written appeal to HR within 10 business days of receiving the review. 2. HR will review the appeal and may conduct a meeting with the employee and manager. 3. A final decision will be communicated within 15 business days.
Appeal: An employee believes they were rated unfairly. They submit an appeal, and HR conducts a review, ultimately upholding the original rating but providing additional feedback.
New employees will undergo a probationary review to assess fit and performance.
Employees transferring to new roles will have a review based on their previous performance and new role expectations.
Employees on extended leave will have their reviews postponed until they return, with adjustments made based on the duration of absence.

Before Reviews: Schedule review meetings. Gather performance data. Prepare feedback. During Reviews: Discuss performance openly. Document feedback. Set future goals. After Reviews: Submit completed forms to HR. Follow up on development plans.

1. What if I disagree with my performance rating? You can submit an appeal to HR within 10 business days. 2. How often should I have feedback sessions with my manager? Regular checkins are encouraged at least once a month. 3. What happens if I am on leave during the review period? Your review will be postponed until your return. 4. Can I set my own goals? Yes, but they must align with company objectives and be reviewed by your manager. 5. What if I receive a low rating? A performance improvement plan will be developed to help you address the issues. 6. Are there training opportunities linked to my performance review? Yes, development needs identified in reviews will be linked to training programs. 7. How are promotions determined? Promotions are based on performance ratings, contributions, and alignment with company needs. 8. What documentation is required for my performance review? Completed review forms, goalsetting forms, and notes from feedback sessions. 9. How does the calibration committee work? They ensure consistency in performance ratings across departments. 10. What if I have further questions about the policy? Contact your HR representative for clarification.

#### Promotion Scenario Context: An employee consistently exceeds expectations. Action: The manager documents achievements, aligns goals with company strategy, and recommends the employee for promotion during the annual review. #### Underperformance Scenario Context: An employee struggles to meet deadlines. Action: The manager implements a PIP, providing resources and regular feedback. After three months, the employee shows improvement and meets expectations. #### Appeal Scenario Context: An employee feels their rating is unfair. Action: They submit an appeal, and HR facilitates a meeting. After reviewing evidence, HR upholds the rating but offers additional support for development.
